fr:title.text: Context-Sensitive Persona Control for LLM Agents

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Context-Sensitive Persona Control for LLM Agents

html:ul.html:li: Studying how stable persona constraints can induce context-sensitive behavior in LLM agents, rather than being expressed uniformly across situations.
Developing a training-free framework that dynamically identifies situation-relevant attributes and retrieves behavioral evidence to compile persona specifications into agent behavior.
Extending the framework toward a modular agent architecture that separates stable persona, transient internal state, and episodic memory.

fr:title.text: AI Reasoning Verification: Stepwise Verification via NLI

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: AI Reasoning Verification: Stepwise Verification via NLI

html:ul.html:li: Reframed stepwise reasoning verification as local Natural Language Inference (NLI), employing fair comparison of language models with different architectures and training paradigms.
Results showed that discriminative supervision consistently outperforms generative verdict training across both encoder and decoder LMs. (Supported by the Alan Turing Institute).

fr:title.text: Representation vs. Execution: SFT and RL under Distribution Shift

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Representation vs. Execution: SFT and RL under Distribution Shift

html:ul.html:li: Investigated post-training dynamics (SFT vs. GRPO) under distributional shifts on Qwen2.5-1.5B using Structural Causal Models and layer-wise linear probing.
Demonstrated that outcome-based RL restores syntactic compliance (98.2%) while latent causal rules remain internally encoded (66% probe accuracy) despite generative execution failure.

fr:title.text: Sparse Feature Circuits in Sycophantic Behaviour

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Sparse Feature Circuits in Sycophantic Behaviour

html:ul.html:li: Applied Sparse Feature Circuits (SFC) and SHIFT framework with JumpReLU SAEs (Gemma Scope) on Gemma-2-2B to analyze model sycophancy across NLP, Philosophy, and Political domains.
Showed that targeted ablation of 10^2 - 10^3 sparse features reduces sycophancy rates from 85.2% to 45.2% with minimal capability degradation.

fr:title.text: Multi-Agent RL: Algorithm for Sequential Social Dilemmas

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Multi-Agent RL: Algorithm for Sequential Social Dilemmas

html:ul.html:li: Reproduced and extended MARL pipelines for sequential social dilemmas in XuanCe, including MeltingPot integration, visual-observation support, prosocial reward sharing, and the MOCA contract-augmentation framework.

Evaluated multiple MARL methods across MPE, MeltingPot, and CleanUp; MAPPO exceeded the original single-agent PPO baseline on CleanUp by 69.3% (2-agent) and 94.8% (4-agent), with reproduced MOCA yielding additional gains over separate training.
